items.titleEn: Can gold hold $4,000 with an October rate hike still in play?
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Hotter-than-expected consumer prices have put an October rate hike back in play , pushing real bond yields higher and dragging gold prices below a critical near-term support level. However, commodity analysts expect support to continue to hold at $4,000 an ounce, as the Federal Reserve is unlikely to raise interest rates just one week before American voters head to the polls for the 2026 midterm elections. In a note Wednesday, Ryan McKay, Director of Commodity Strategy at TD Securities, noted that gold’s inability to break through resistance at $4,200 has prompted speculative fund managers to liquidate their long positions, while the disappointing inflation numbers have added fuel to the fire.

U.S. Treasury's gold revaluation could restart the ‘debasement trade' as yield pressures fade – UBP's Kinsella
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Gold has likely seen the worst of its Treasury-yield-driven losses, and once the Iran situation improves and Fed rate hike expectations ease, the Treasury department itself could provide a new tailwind for bullion prices between now and year-end, according to Peter Kinsella, Head of Investment Services for the UK at Swiss private bank UBP. Kinsella noted that gold has traded lower since the Federal Reserve’s 25-basis-point rate hike in September. “The downward move has been rather muted, considering the huge rise in both nominal and real inflation-adjusted interest rates,” he said. “US 10-year yields have risen to highs of 5.30%, and 10-year TIPS yields (a proxy for real interest rate expectations) have risen to levels of just below 3%.”

Gold, silver drop as hotter CPI revives Fed-rate pressure - Kitco AM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) – Spot gold and silver prices are sharply lower in early U.S. trading Wednesday, after hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation data revived concerns that energy-driven price pressure will keep the Federal Reserve’s year-end tightening path in place. At the time of writing, spot gold was trading near $4,110.90 an ounce, down 1.18% on the session, while spot silver was trading near $57.890, down 1.97%. Market positioning shifted back toward the hawkish side after September CPI rose 0.6% on the month and 3.7% from a year earlier , above the 3.6% consensus and up from 3.4% in August. Core CPI rose 0.3% on the month and 2.6% year over year, while gasoline rose 9.1% and the energy index climbed 5.2%, showing that the oil shock is feeding directly into headline inflation. The print does not make an October hike the base case, but it reinforces the December-hike channel that was already heavily priced after Fed minutes showed most officials still expected another increase by year-end. The 10-year Treasury yield was trading near the 5.2% area and the dollar index was off Monday’s 18-month high but firm enough to pressure metals. The next tests are Thursday’s PPI, retail sales, jobless claims and Philadelphia Fed survey, followed by Friday’s import and export prices and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s IMF appearance. Softer producer prices or weak spending would help gold by limiting real-rate pressure; a firm PPI or retail-sales print would keep the dollar and yields pointed against bullion.

items.titleEn: Gold price drops to session lows as U.S. CPI heats up in September
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold prices have fallen to session lows, testing critical support as hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation data reinforces expectations that the Federal Reserve will have to raise interest rates by year-end, increasing the opportunity cost of holding the non-yielding precious metal. At the same time, higher energy prices are becoming embedded in the broader economy, which some economists have said could force interest rates to remain higher for longer. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose by 0.6% last month, following August’s 0.4% increase, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics announced Wednesday. The monthly inflation data came in line with market expectations.
